questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to inspect processes and time-based conditions from /proc with POSIX tools, focusing on runtime security and privilege boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- /proc/[pid]/status Uid fields (real vs. effective)
- /proc/[pid]/stat starttime and clock ticks
- /proc/uptime and getconf CLK_TCK for time calculations
- Mapping UID to usernames via getent

## Code Example
```bash
#!/bin/sh
uptime=$(cat /proc/uptime | awk '{print $1}')
clk=$(getconf CLK_TCK)
for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do
  [ -r "$p/status" ] || continue
  ruid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $2}' "$p/status" 2>/dev/null)
  euid=$(awk '/^Uid:/ {print $3}' "$p/status" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$ruid" ] || continue
  st=$(awk '{print $22}' "$p/stat" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$st" ] || continue
  age=$(( (uptime - (st/clk)) ))
  [ "$euid" != "$ruid" ] && [ "$age" -le 300 ] && cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < "$p/cmdline" 2>/dev/null)
  user=$(getent passwd "$ruid" | cut -d: -f1)
  printf "%s %s %s %s %s\n" "${p##*/}" "$user" "$cmd" "$euid" "$ruid"
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would this adapt to cgroups or containers?
- What race conditions or permission issues arise, and how would you mitigate them?

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to reason about stale PIDs, unreadable files, and craft robust one-liners with standard UNIX tools. Demonstrates safe parsing, process existence checks, and resilient file handling.

## Key Concepts

- POSIX shell loops and pipelines
- /proc existence checks
- Safe PID extraction
- Handling unreadable files

## Code Example

```bash
find /var/run -name '*.pid' -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do \
    pid=$(head -n1 "$f" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]'); \
    if [ -n "$pid" ] && [ ! -d "/proc/$pid" ]; then \
      svc=$(basename "$f" .pid); \
      printf "%s %s %s\n" "$svc" "$pid" "$(stat -c '%y' "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; \
    fi; \
  done | sort
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you monitor this script output over time and alert on a rising stale PID count?

## Why This Is Asked
Probes practical Unix security instincts: identify risky file permissions that could enable privilege escalation. The command must robustly traverse the filesystem, skip transient pseudo-filesystems, and present a concise summary for audits.

## Key Concepts
- find with pruning to avoid /proc, /sys, /dev
- -perm checks for SUID/SGID/world-writable
- stat to display permissions, owner, group, and path
- 2>/dev/null to ignore unreadable paths
- sort for deterministic output

## Code Example
```bash
find / -path /proc -prune -o -path /sys -prune -o -path /dev -prune -o -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 -o -perm -0002 \) -print 2>/dev/null | while read -r p; do stat -c '%A %U %G %p' "$p"; done | sort
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you restrict the search to a known set of mount points?
- How would you integrate this into a nightly audit with alerting when new risky files appear?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to handle mixed log formats, gzipped archives, and nested paths, while producing precise per-hour, per-service aggregates in a single pass.

## Key Concepts
- Robust parsing for text and JSON lines without external libs
- Decompressing .gz on the fly (zcat) and skipping unreadable files
- Deriving service from path or JSON field
- Time bucketing by hour and rolling window (12h)
- Streaming aggregation with POSIX AWK

## Code Example
```bash
find /logs -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.log.gz' \) -print0 | \
  xargs -0 -I{} sh -lc 'f="{}"; case "${f##*.}" in gz) zcat "$f" 2>/dev/null || true ;; *) cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac' | \
  awk 'BEGIN{FS=""; OFS=","}
       /\[|{"ts":/ {/* parse via simple regex; normalize to ts,lvl,service */}
       }' 2>/dev/null | \
  sort -u | \
  awk 'BEGIN{FS=",";OFS=","} {hour=substr($1,1,13)"0"; service=$2; count[$hour","$service]+=($3=="ERROR"||$3=="CRITICAL")} END{for(k in count) print k","count[k]}' | \
  sort
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for a real-time streaming feed instead of a 12h batch window?
- How would you test correctness with skewed clocks and missing timestamps?
